title: PhenoPhaseR: Reproducible processing workflow for interpolating phenological DWD observations
description:
PhenoPhaseR is a reproducible R workflow for downloading, filtering, modelling, and spatially interpolating phenological observations provided by the German Weather Service (DWD). It implements the PHASE approach (Gerstmann et al. 2016), combining growing-degree-day models with geostatistical interpolation to produce area-wide phenological predictions across Germany at 1 km spatial resolution, and publishes its outputs as FAIR Digital Objects (RO-Crate 1.2) with PROV-O provenance, DCAT/Dublin Core descriptors, and honestly anchored DQV data-quality metadata.

v1.9.1 — registered-route measure concepts; propagated-uncertainty terms; fairagrodq 0.3.0. A patch release for the pipeline: the RO-Crates it emits are unchanged, because no PhenoPhaseR measurement uses the added terms. tools/generate_fairagrodq_ttl.R now emits every registry measure carrying a fairagrodq:-owned dimension as a dqv:Metric/skos:Concept node with skos:definition, dqv:inDimension and, where the measure's basis maps onto one, fairagrodq:expressedBy. This completes the registered route: the vocabulary previously published dimensions and expression principles but not the measures that use them, so a measure IRI emitted in a crate did not resolve. Three propagated-uncertainty measures (u_pheno, u_precip, u_total) are registered, each declaring dct:isDefinedBy WeatherIndicatoR (10.5281/zenodo.19631197), together with a propagated basis label rendered as “analytical error propagation (model-asserted, unvalidated)”. The generated vocabulary is now vendored as fairagrodq.ttl (v0.3.0) so its terms are readable without running R and drift is visible in a diff. The https://w3id.org/fairagro/dq# namespace now resolves; the terms remain project-defined and are still not part of ISO 19157-1.

v1.9.0 — honest validation basis for every accuracy metric. The emitted metadata no longer conflates hold-out, in-sample and deviance-explained results under a single label. Every measure in the registry records the regime that produced it (basis) and, where a number is optimistically biased, a caveat; both builders read their metric descriptions from that one source, so descriptions can no longer diverge across crates. New tokens is_rmse / is_mae / is_cor carry the in-sample critical_doy_determination() metrics honestly. No data files change — re-emit crate metadata against the unchanged data.

v1.8.0 — honest anchoring of spatially explicit uncertainty. The spatial-uncertainty quality dimensions were migrated from dffp: to the fairagrodq: namespace and declare dct:isDefinedBy Säurich et al. (2026) rather than asserting conformance to ISO 19157-1, which contains no Spatial-Uncertainty element. An orthogonal expression-principle axis (fairagrodq:UncertaintyExpressionPrinciple, reached via fairagrodq:expressedBy) records how each uncertainty was produced and what it may claim, so a consumer can distinguish model-asserted from empirically-validated uncertainty. Already-published crates keep their original IRIs as historical record.
